import html # A minimal HTML template for a forum post. # {poster}, {heading}, {body} are placeholders for the main content. # {labels} will contain a series of elements representing tags. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{heading}

Posted by: {poster}

{body}
{labels}
""" def create_forum_post(poster: str, heading: str, body: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster : str Author of the post. heading : str Title of the post. body : str Main content of the post. labels : list[str] Tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str A fully escaped HTML string safe for rendering in a browser. Raises ------ TypeError If any of the arguments are not of the expected type. """ # Validate argument types if not isinstance(poster, str): raise TypeError("poster must be a string") if not isinstance(heading, str): raise TypeError("heading must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise TypeError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(labels, list) or not all(isinstance(l, str) for l in labels): raise TypeError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape all user-supplied content to prevent XSS and injection. safe_poster = html.escape(poster, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(heading, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=False) # body may contain line breaks # Build tag spans; each tag is escaped and wrapped in a . safe_tags = ' '.join(f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in labels) # Format the final HTML string. return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster=safe_poster, heading=safe_heading, body=safe_body.replace('\n', '
'), # preserve line breaks labels=safe_tags )
